## RiskRuleSeverity

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Execution.Sdk.RiskRuleSeverity</code>. Kind: `enum`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs:20](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs#L20).

How seriously a rule treats its own findings. This is the single lever that decides admission. The validator maps it to an outcome and no rule can override that mapping per order, so a rule&#x27;s declared severity and its effect can never disagree. Lives here rather than in Meridian.Risk because RiskViolation carries it and Meridian.Execution&#x27;s RiskValidationResult exposes those violations. Meridian.Risk references Meridian.Execution, so the reverse reference would be a project cycle.

```csharp
public enum RiskRuleSeverity
```

## RiskViolation

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Execution.Sdk.RiskViolation</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs:76](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs#L76).

A breach attributed to the rule that raised it, as the validator records it. Constructed by the validator, which is what guarantees Severity is the declaring rule&#x27;s own and not a value chosen per order.

```csharp
public sealed record RiskViolation(string RuleName, RiskRuleSeverity Severity, string Code, string Message, decimal? ObservedValue = null, decimal? LimitValue = null, bool RequiresAcknowledgement = false)
```

| <code>public bool IsBlocking =&gt; …;</code> | [src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs:95](../../../../src/Meridian.Execution.Sdk/RiskContracts.cs#L95) | True when this violation is one that blocks. Derived from Severity so it can never disagree with the validator&#x27;s own admission logic. Stated as &quot;not explicitly non-blocking&quot; rather than &quot;Error or Critical&quot;. A C# enum can hold any value of its underlying type — a cast or a numeric deserialization in host code is enough — and this is a public SDK contract on a fail-closed gate. Listing the blocking severities would admit an unrecognised one with warnings; listing the safe ones rejects it. |
